subject: Clarify: audit coverage cutoff, log capture instants, and evidence deliverables
messages:
From: Simon Taylor <simon.taylor@brightline-audit.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II – coverage cutoff and point-in-time evidence

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the evidence packet. As we prepare the Type II procedures for Acme, a couple of scope details need clarification before we map our sampling plan:

1) Report period end: our working files show the report period ends 2027-05-31 (inclusive). Can you confirm whether Redwood treats the day as inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC or if there is any local-time cutoff we should be aware of?

2) Point-in-time/system snapshot evidence: For items that are captured as "daily snapshots" (configs, queued job states, DB exports), what exact timestamp is used for the snapshot (e.g. 2027-05-31T23:59:00 PST)? We need the authoritative capture instant so we can classify traces as "in period" vs "post-period."

3) Logs spanning the boundary: Acme is asking whether rolling logs that include events from 2027-05-31 23:58 through 2027-06-01 00:02 will be considered in-scope for the May period if the log file is named after the start date. If you have a recommended naming/timestamping convention or a SOC-friendly manifest, that helps.

4) Bridge letter: if there is any gap in evidence (e.g., a delayed export), would Redwood consider providing a short bridge letter stating the reason for any missing artifact and the remedial evidence? If yes, what is the typical timeline to produce one?

Could you reply with the canonical answers and, where possible, attach the single-file artifacts we should pull for our sampling (config snapshot, manifest, and a small log sample)? That will let us finalize the test matrix.

Appreciate it — we want to minimize rework during the fieldwork next week.

Best,
Simon
Simon Taylor
Manager, IT Assurance
Brightline Audit

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Simon Taylor <simon.taylor@brightline-audit.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II – coverage cutoff and point-in-time evidence

Hi Simon,

Quick answers up front, details below:
- Report period end: 2027-05-31 is inclusive. Our canonical policy is that day ends at 23:59:59 UTC for audit purposes.
- Snapshot timestamp: daily system/config snapshots are taken at 23:55 UTC and recorded with UTC timestamps.
- Logs: we keep event-level timestamps in UTC; log files may roll at local midnight for some services but every event has a UTC timestamp and our manifest maps events to UTC instants.
- Bridge letters: yes, we can provide a bridge letter for narrowly scoped gaps; typical turnaround is 48–72 hours after we confirm the missing artifact and cause.

Detailed context:
1) Cutoff semantics — We run a global cutoff for evidence classification at 23:59:59 UTC on the final day of the period. This applies to the evidence index we produce for auditors. Some subsystem log rotation occurs on local time (PST/PDT) to avoid heavy I/O during maintenance windows, but rotation metadata contains the UTC boundaries so you can map events.

2) Snapshot process — The infra team runs an automated config and metadata snapshot job at 23:55 UTC. That job publishes a tarball to the secured evidence bucket and writes an entry to the evidence manifest with the exact UTC timestamp and SHA256. We will attach the manifest and one sample snapshot for May 31.

3) Log file naming vs event timestamps — File names historically follow the service-local-date (e.g., access-2027-05-31.log), but each line/event includes an ISO8601 UTC timestamp. For your sampling you should rely on event timestamps rather than file names; our manifest includes a crosswalk between file ranges and event UTC ranges.

4) Bridge letters — We maintain a short draft template for bridge letters; if auditors require one we can sign and return within 48–72 hours. They include: the artifact identifier, reason (e.g., "rotation delay due to DB failover"), affected UTC instants, and remedial artifacts (e.g., from backup snapshots).

I'll attach the following to this thread: a short manifest extract, one config snapshot tarball (redacted for customer data), an example log slice spanning 2027-05-31T23:58:00Z → 2027-06-01T00:02:00Z, and the bridge-letter template. Priyom and Marcus are on copy to confirm the snapshots and retention excerpt.

Action items for you: please confirm that explicit acceptance of UTC 23:59:59 as the authoritative cutoff satisfies your classification. If you need a signed bridge letter in advance (e.g., to accept samples retroactively), let us know and we can prepare the draft.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Head of Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0192

Attachments referenced: SOC2_TypeII_2027-05-report-request.pdf (request), config_snapshot_20270531.tar.gz (sample), access_logs_20270530-20270601.csv (log slice), retention_policy_excerpt.pdf

From: Simon Taylor <simon.taylor@brightline-audit.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II – coverage cutoff and point-in-time evidence

Thanks, Chloe — that is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups:

- We accept UTC 23:59:59 as the period cutoff. Please ensure the manifest explicitly states the UTC capture instant for the config snapshot (we'll reference the SHA).

- For audit sampling we typically request: the manifest (machine-readable CSV/JSON), the snapshot tarball hash, and a short note describing retention/overwrite windows for backups that might affect reconstitution. Can you provide the retention policy excerpt for the relevant S3 bucket and the DB export retention window?

- Bridge letter question: Acme's InfoSec has asked whether the bridge letter can be produced at the time of evidence delivery (i.e., included in the audit packet) or must be separately signed later. If you can include a draft now, that would save time.

Please attach the three items you referenced and, if possible, a short statement from infrastructure confirming the 23:55 UTC snapshot schedule — that will be sufficient for our control testing.

Simon

On a side note: for the log sample you supplied, we will use event timestamps; thanks for clarifying the crosswalk.

Priyom / Chloe / Simon,

Confirming details from infra:
- Snapshot job: 23:55:00 UTC daily (cron: 55 23 * * *). On failure the job retries twice at +5 minute intervals; the manifest records the actual completion timestamp and the SHA256 of the produced tarball. The manifest field is "capture_utc" and contains full ISO8601 timestamps (e.g., 2027-05-31T23:55:12Z).

- Manifest format (CSV header): artifact_id, capture_utc, sha256, size_bytes, s3_uri, environment, note
  Example manifest row (redacted): redwood-config-20270531,2027-05-31T23:55:12Z,3a7b...e9f,10485760,s3://evidence-prod/soc2/2027/05/redwood-config-20270531.tar.gz,prod,"daily-config-snapshot"

- Evidence location: s3://evidence-prod/soc2/2027/05/ (public manifest exported to auditors' secure share after access request)

- DB export retention: on-disk exports are kept for 14 days before lifecycle to cold storage (Glacier-equivalent) for 1 year; restoration windows are 24–72 hours depending on archive size. We'll include the retention excerpt from the policy.

I've attached the requested sample artifacts to this reply: config_snapshot_20270531.tar.gz (redacted), access_logs_20270530-20270601.csv (sliced), retention_policy_excerpt.pdf. Let me know if you need a separate signed statement — we can provide one.

Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
